A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DARS research work. All 18 pages of v5 and 26 pages of v7, including their appendices, are readable, and the text, equations, tables and rendered figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V5 reports original RLVR experiments, including mathematical benchmark results, training dynamics and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V7 retains those original experiments and adds results for non-mathematical tasks, majority voting, static difficulty allocation, training time and rollout-cap annealing.

M1.justification: The core two-stage DARS sampler, ET/HW allocation rules and training loss are retained. V7 Appendix G.2 instantiates and tests a cap-annealed variant: Nmax stays at 64 for 200 steps, then decreases linearly to 16. V5 Appendix F.2 discussed gradual cap reduction only as future work.

E1.justification: V5's empirical coverage is mathematical reasoning. V7 Appendix E.1 and Table 5 additionally evaluate the mathematics-trained Qwen checkpoints on GPQA-Diamond scientific reasoning and HumanEval code generation, substantially broadening domain and task coverage. Existing mathematical training and evaluation datasets are retained.

E2.justification: V7 adds Static DARS, which freezes difficulty-based rollout budgets estimated using the initial model, alongside the RLVR baseline, Depth-Naive and online DARS-HW in Table 6. Existing comparator sets are otherwise retained. GRPO/RLVR label changes are renaming; MaxRL is compared theoretically, not experimentally.

E3.justification: V7 adds majority-vote evaluation using maj@8 and maj@16, 64-response evaluations on the new domains, a frozen-difficulty control, and a fixed-cap versus annealed-cap training experiment. These substantially extend the evaluation design. The original main-experiment budgets, metrics, temperature settings and checkpoint-selection rules remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether online difficulty adaptation matters relative to static allocation, investigate the proposed cap-annealing tradeoff, and compare generated reasoning traces in an AIME24 case study. The temperature sweep, standard-deviation-based advantage ablation, checkpoint averages and response-length analyses already appeared in v5 and are retained or relocated.

E5.justification: V7 Section 4.4 and Table 3 newly report majority-vote results averaged over five independent sampling rounds. V5 reported response sampling and averages across three checkpoints, but no corresponding repeated-round evaluation. Neither version reports training-seed replication or confidence intervals; the new MaxRL variance analysis is theoretical.

E6.justification: Existing main and retained appendix scores are unchanged after matching merged and renumbered tables. V7 adds majority-vote, transfer, static-allocation, timing, annealing and case-study results. For example, Table 5 reports 1.5B HumanEval Avg@64 of 49.5 for DARS-HW-Breadth versus 41.1 for RLVR. Table 11 reports Pass@1/128 of 50.9/80.6 with annealing versus 50.0/82.1 with a fixed cap; these are newly reported comparisons under different schedules.

T1.justification: V5 Appendix C's gradient-norm upper-bound derivation is removed. V7 adds propositions deriving idealized ET log-odds and HW maximum-likelihood objectives, followed by expected-gradient and variance comparisons with MaxRL in Appendices B.2 and C. Equation 7 also changes 2(1-x_j) to 2x_j, resolving its inconsistency with the HW allocation already specified in v5 Equation 8 and Appendix B.

C1.justification: The central claims about cumulative-advantage bias, DARS and complementary depth/breadth gains remain. V7 adds an explicit introduction-level contribution claiming that ET and HW recover log-odds and maximum-likelihood objectives, respectively, extending the contribution statement without replacing the paper's central thesis.

C2.justification: V7 adds substantive interpretations of DARS-HW as a variance-reduced route to maximum-likelihood optimization, online allocation as tracking policy-dependent difficulty, and transfer results as evidence of applicability beyond mathematics. The annealing discussion now interprets an observed Pass@1–Pass@128 tradeoff. Appendix B.2 also states the idealized population, uncapped and continuous assumptions underlying the objective interpretation.

D1.justification: V7 Appendix D newly describes VERL serving backends such as vLLM, continuous batching and asynchronous scheduling. Table 4 adds measured time per training step to v5's rollout-count information. These are additional disclosures; the PDFs do not establish a backend switch. Existing code access, hardware, prompts, preprocessing and core hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: V7 substantially positions DARS-HW relative to MaxRL through a new formal comparison claiming a shared objective but different sampling and variance behavior. It also adds Focal Loss as motivation for emphasizing difficult examples. These relationships were absent from v5, although the broader RLVR literature discussion is largely retained.

P1.justification: V7 substantially reorganizes the experimental narrative into separate training-dynamics, test-time scaling, ablation, temperature, efficiency and complete-curve subsections. It moves the temperature discussion into the main text, adds an appendix contents guide and reorganizes the theory, case-study and discussion sections. Much of the original abstract and method prose remains.

P2.justification: V7 places v5 Figure 8 on the opening page as Figure 1 and merges v5 Tables 1 and 3 into Table 2. It relocates the temperature heatmap and depth-training curves between the main text and appendices, reformats and extends the rollout-cost table, and adds theoretical and experimental tables plus a case-study figure. These are substantial display and layout changes.

improvement.justification: V7 strengthens support for adaptive allocation and practical usefulness through the static control, science/code evaluations, majority-vote tests and measured step times. The gain is qualified: the replacement theory is idealized, checkpoint selection remains asymmetric in Section 4.1, and the new successful-answer case contains invalid intermediate reasoning, including sqrt(84.5)=13/2 in Figure 17. The additional empirical evidence supports a limited net quality improvement.
